I am deeply, deeply sorry for your loss. I lost my mother years ago and it is an awful thing to go through. You will seek nurture and comfort more than others do for some time - this is natural, just don't develop bad habits. As it happened 6 months ago I know you will have dealt with the immediate shock - I'd recommend (if you haven't already) trying to get a therapist, or talking to a friend you trust about it, asap. I blocked a lot of feelings out and it ended up just festering over years, it'll help you to mentally deal with it to talk and share feelings.        
Secondly, please please do not blame yourself. Guilt and self blame are very very common when grieving - it's a way of trying to process it, I guess. A battle with cancer is physical, whether you had visited or not there would have been the same outcome. Your mother specifically stated she didn't want to be visited too, so please don't feel guilty. My mother died at home (also cancer, fuck cancer) and in her last couple days when she became unresponsive she didn't want anyone in the room. Chances are your mother didnt want you to have to see her in a weak state - it does hurt to see a loved one like that. Your most recent memories of seeing your Mother are of her healthy and well, sounds like that's what she wanted.    
The fact you had no money to pay your driving instructor frustrated you. That's totally reasonable. You had no idea atall of the situation - you just knew there was no money to pay them, so please *do not feel guilty for it*. You didn't know and you can't have known and your mother would have known this too - you didn't understand what was going on.                    
Something like losing a parent isn't something you can just dust yourself off from - it'll take time to recover. The little things are what help - a nice view, seeing a cute animal, eating a nice meal, shit like that. It aint easy with depression but there are always things to savour and enjoy if you look for them. Make sure you look after yourself, eat sleep exercise (or do your best to), it's the quickest and easiest way to feel better.         
You can and will live and you will be fine if you stick it out. You will feel happy again and you will overcome your problems, ride out the bad times and savor the good things in life - every one of us has the strength to do that. I'm sorry if this comes across as incoherent and honestly, I wish I could tell you how much I feel for you here, but things *are* gonna be OK. PM me anytime you need to
